claim_blocks.paragraph: OONI anomaly index reports 57.5 percent across 245,046 completed measurements, OONI in-path middlebox index reports 1.29 percent across 9,681 completed middlebox tests, and Inside-China fixed DNS panel reports 1.0 ratio across 5 qualifying answered measurement domains. The three cited values do not share a population, protocol, test family, denominator, or even a common unit, while measurements with the same independence-group identifier count only once. The cited measurements record observable interference within their named methods, but they cannot be combined into one defensible national filtering percentage.

countercases.disposition: Retained; the report claims observable interference, not that every anomaly is a confirmed block.

evidence.interpretation_limit: OONI's anomaly index uses completed measurements across several test families; the separate total-measurement count also includes failed attempts. An anomaly is not a confirmed block and the probe/test mix is not China's population.
evidence.title: OONI anomaly index

evidence.interpretation_limit: This is derived from OONI measurements and shares the publisher:ooni lineage. Its completed-test denominator and test family differ from the OONI reachability index.
evidence.title: OONI in-path middlebox index

evidence.interpretation_limit: The ratio is for a fixed, deliberately censorship-sensitive domain panel and consented cloud probes; it is not a representative domain or user sample.
evidence.title: Inside-China fixed DNS panel

falsifiers.statement: The observable-interference finding would weaken if independently operated China and control vantages converged within instrument error across repeated windows.
falsifiers.test: Repeat predeclared protocols over multiple windows and compare China/control distributions with retained raw denominators.

falsifiers.statement: A national-rate estimate would become testable only after a representative sampling frame and common outcome definition exist.
falsifiers.test: Publish the sampling frame, inclusion probabilities, shared protocol, nonresponse accounting and uncertainty interval before estimating a population rate.

hypotheses.statement: Network interference affecting China-facing tests is observable across independently produced measurement methods.
The 3 headline values estimate one common national filtering rate.

limitations.consequence: No weighted average or single national percentage is calculated.
limitations.statement: The instruments observe different test populations with different denominators and units.

limitations.consequence: Findings are bounded to the named instruments and collection windows.
limitations.statement: Probe, resolver, domain and remote-vantage coverage is not a probability sample of China's people or networks.

limitations.consequence: They count as one independent group at the publication gate.
limitations.statement: OONI reachability and in-path metrics reuse the same publisher lineage.

limitations.consequence: An available source is not republished or counted when its current contract permits metadata-only reuse.

methodology.description: Hash the exact four public input files and validate their declared schemas.

Resolve independence groups through the evidence mesh before counting corroboration.
Require complete sentence citations, fresh evidence, independent groups and adversarial review.
